contract.words: Get $2,500 into my account within 21 days without spending anything up front. I won't do any of the work myself — Brain or someone it hires has to do all of it.

terms.proofCondition: $2,500 settled in the owner's account within 21 days, with no up-front spend; all work done by Brain or a hired provider.

strategy.title: Free cold email selling $1,500 prepaid website rebuilds, built by a freelancer paid out of each settled sale
strategy.why: The only discovered route that needs no up-front money and no owner work: buyers prepay, the freelancer is paid only from settled payouts, and three sales by day 7 settle by day 21 under Stripe's 7-14 day first-payout rule. Demand, price acceptance, close rate and the freelancer's price are unmeasured, so a day-7 test decides it.

alternatives.title: One-time Google Business Profile optimization at $250
alternatives.why: 17 prepaid sales needed by day 7 to settle in time; same unmeasured close rate with 6x the volume

alternatives.title: Upwork or Fiverr marketplace work
alternatives.why: Upwork may require an up-front Connects purchase for new freelancers (forbidden spend) and an owner-held verified account; Fiverr's clearance after completion pushes first cash past day 21

steps.label: Build a list of US local service businesses with no/outdated website from free public directories and send cold email from a free mailbox to 500 of them (days 1-5)
Offer a fixed-scope 5-page website rebuild at $1,500, paid 100% up front by Stripe payment link before any work is bought
Validation: count paid orders from the 500 contacts by day 7
Take payment for 3 rebuilds by day 7 through the Stripe payment link (Brain answers replies)
Stripe payouts to the owner's bank: first payout 7-14 days after the first payment
Freelance web designer builds each site at a fixed $600, engaged and paid only after that sale's payout has settled

Build a list of US local service businesses with no/outdated website from free public directories and send cold email from the free mailbox (CAN-SPAM sender identity and postal address included) to 500 of them at ~100 per day, days 2-6

Stripe payouts to the owner's bank: first payout 7-14 days after the first payment (days 19-21 at the latest)

stop: Fewer than 3 paid orders by day 7 - stop: later sales cannot settle by day 21; nothing has been spent

answers.finding: MAJOR: 'Rebuild in 7 days' vs freelancer engaged only after payout (days 19-21) -> delivery ~day 26-28; restate the promise and count dispute/refund risk before day 21.
answers.resolution: Accepted. The offer now promises delivery within 21 days of payment (freelancer engaged on payout day, 7-day build, latest delivery day 28 for a day-7 sale); the test measures conversion at that promise; refund/dispute rate is an UNKNOWN quantity and a refund before day 21 that drops settled cash below $2,500 is a stop condition.

answers.finding: MAJOR: Freelancer quote required 'before the first payment link' but no step obtains it and the stop refunds after payment; add the quote step before s2.
answers.resolution: Accepted. New step s1 (day 1) obtains a written fixed quote <= $600 with a 7-day build starting on payout day and a work sample; the offer step depends on it, and the stop rule now sends no offer (nothing to refund) if no such quote exists by day 2.

answers.finding: MINOR: members lists the rejected GBP alternative.
answers.resolution: Rebutted. Brain's check requires `members` arithmetic for every opening weighed in `chain` (ARITHMETIC_UNSTATED otherwise); the GBP opening is a weighed alternative, not a plan member, and strategy.opportunityIds names only cop_9f38af0ae8614ccf8a86.

answers.finding: NOTE: Stripe account/bank verification and the sending mailbox need the owner's identity once; name it as the owner's only action.
answers.resolution: Accepted. Step s0 names it as the owner's only action: identity verification for Stripe, its bank payout and the mailbox - no delivery or sales work.

answers.finding: NOTE: 500 cold emails over 5 days from a brand-new free mailbox risks deliverability and the provider's bulk-mail terms, and a CAN-SPAM sender address is required; the day-7 gate could stop a viable offer for that reason.
answers.resolution: Accepted. Sending is spread at ~100/day over days 2-6 with individually written messages, sender identity and postal address included for CAN-SPAM; the risk that deliverability stops a viable offer is stated - the zero-spend cap rules out paid sending tools.

answers.finding: NOTE: Price $1,500 and the reach basis rest on sources I verified do not establish this buyer's price or a reachable count (cnd_6acbd368f8804c068d69, cnd_199de8755eb04f648b79); acceptable only as what the test measures.
answers.resolution: Accepted. Price stays an ESTIMATE and OFFER_AND_PRICE and CURRENT_DEMAND are in validation.decides; the test measures them.

answers.finding: FULFILMENT condition
answers.resolution: The card's fulfillment is a RECOMMENDATION and Brain's FULFILMENT link is false; s1 now secures the quote, start date and sample before any offer, and FULFILMENT stays in validation.decides.

reviews.reasons: CONDITIONAL is the right family and the money arithmetic holds: 3 x $1,500 = $4,500; Stripe fees 3 x $43.80 = $131.40; freelancer 3 x $600 = $1,800; net $2,568.60 >= $2,500 (trace netCents 256860), $0 up front, payouts days 19-21 under Stripe's 7-14 day first-payout rule, and the gate (3 paid of 500 by day 7) carries exactly the 3 sales needed. But it cannot run as written. (1) The offer contradicts the plan's own fulfilment timing and invites refunds: buyers prepay $1,500 for a 'rebuild in 7 days' on days 5-7, but the freelancer is engaged only after that sale's payout settles (days 19-21), so sites arrive ~days 26-28, about three weeks late; a dispute or refund request before day 21 removes the cash the target rests on, and the ledger counts refunds at $0. With exposure capped at $0 the freelancer cannot be paid earlier, so the offer must promise delivery after payout (e.g. within ~21 days of payment) and the test must measure conversion at that promise. (2) Orders are taken before fulfilment is shown: Brain's FULFILMENT link is false and the card's fulfillment is a RECOMMENDATION; the plan's own quantity requires a freelancer's written fixed quote <= $600 'before the first payment link is sent', yet no step obtains it before s2 (day 2), and the stop branch still reads 'No freelancer quotes $600 or less - refund every payment and stop', i.e. after payments. Add a step that gets the quote (with a start date after the payout) before s2. (3) members still carries the rejected GBP alternative (cop_1d9d526c1ca4404f893b, 17 deals). (4) Owner zero-work: the Stripe account and its bank payout, and the free sending mailbox, must be opened and verified in the owner's name; that is a one-time identity step only the owner can do (not delivery work), and the plan should name it rather than imply Brain does everything.

reviews.reasons: Both MAJOR findings from my review of rev_0e2dce5e2ada_472e8c are fixed and the plan is a startable CONDITIONAL test inside every limit. (1) Fulfilment before orders: s1 obtains a written fixed quote <= $600 with a 7-day build starting on payout day plus a work sample before any offer, and the stop sends no offer if it is missing by day 2. (2) The promise now matches the cash: delivery within 21 days of payment; sale 1 (day 5) -> payout and freelancer day 19 -> delivered day 26; sale 3 (day 7) -> day 21 -> day 28; refunds/disputes are an UNKNOWN measured in the test with a stop rule. Recomputed: 3 x $1,500 = $4,500 - fees 3 x $43.80 - freelancer 3 x $600 = $2,568.60 (trace netCents 256860) >= $2,500, all settled days 19-21 of 21; owner money at risk $0 (exposure cap $0, every $600 paid from that sale's settled payout); owner work: none in the steps, and the one identity verification of Stripe, bank and mailbox is named as the owner's only action. Gate: 3 paid of 500 by day 7 carries exactly the 3 sales the target needs. members rebuttal accepted (Brain requires arithmetic for every opening weighed in chain; strategy names only cop_9f38af0ae8614ccf8a86).
findings: NOTE: No slack anywhere: one refund or dispute, one sale on day 8, or a first payout later than Stripe's 'typical' 7-14 days misses the target; the stop rules say so, and the owner should read this as a test with a narrow pass band.

strategy.title: Free cold email selling $1,500 prepaid website rebuilds, built by a freelancer paid out of each settled sale
strategy.why: The only discovered route that needs no up-front money and no owner work: buyers prepay, the freelancer is paid only from settled payouts, and three sales by day 7 settle by day 21 under Stripe's 7-14 day first-payout rule. Demand, price acceptance, close rate and the freelancer's price are unmeasured, so a day-7 test decides it. The owner's only action is a one-time identity verification of the Stripe account, its bank payout and the sending mailbox in the owner's name; Brain and the hired freelancer do all sales and delivery work.
